What it solves

Hardly anyone abandons an ERP because a feature is missing

They abandon it because nobody explained what that screen was for, because the project took so long that the business had already changed, or because when something broke there was nobody to call. The software is hardly ever the hard part. The hard part is everything around it, and that's only learned by having done it many times.

  • Implementation projects that outlast the company's patience
  • Systems nobody was taught to use, filled in wrong from day one
  • A vendor who disappears once the install is done
  • Programs that don't talk to each other and force double keying
  • Solutions designed for another country and its tax rules
  • Big vendors who don't return a small customer's call

What is included

What you actually get

We're the ones who build it

The platform is ours. When something needs changing, there's no ticket to raise with a vendor on another continent and no waiting for the next release.

We know the region's tax rules

Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Colombia, Guatemala and Costa Rica. Each with its own tax document, its withholdings and its filings to the relevant authority.

We come from implementing, not from selling

More than a hundred projects delivered before having a product of our own. That decides design choices you don't see in a demo but feel six months in.

We're still there after go-live

Support has a published Service Level Agreement and a channel of its own. The moment a vendor disappears is exactly when they start being needed.

We work with companies of any size

The same system serves a hardware store and a group with several companies. What changes is which modules get switched on.

We also do what isn't our product

Infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, custom development and IT staffing. Sometimes the right answer to a problem isn't selling another module.

How it works

In three steps

  1. We listen to what's failing today

    Before proposing anything. Most of the time, the problem people describe isn't the one costing the most money.

  2. We propose the minimum that solves it

    A module, not a project. If less fixes it, less it is.

  3. We stay

    Go-live is the beginning. What decides whether the system is still used a year from now is what happens afterwards.

In detail

What you notice using it every day

Help is written at the same time as the screen

Every screen ships with its help, its field-by-field explanations and its data dictionary. A screen that isn't explained is a screen that gets filled in wrong.

One customer's data never touches another's

Isolation between subscribers, and between the companies of a single subscriber, is the rule that ranks above every other technical consideration in the project.

One single database, not integrations

Modules don't sync with each other: they read the same data. That difference is what makes it impossible for inventory and accounting to disagree.

The product grows from what's learned in operation

A good part of what the platform does today came out of a real problem from a real customer, not from a competitor's feature list.

We work remotely and on site

The platform runs in the browser, but when a visit is needed, we go. There are customers in five countries and not every problem gets solved over a video call.

What we don't know how to do, we say so

Some jobs don't fit what we're good at. Saying so beforehand costs a sale; not saying so costs a customer and their recommendation.

Who it is for

This is for you if…

If you're about to change systems

It's worth talking to someone who has implemented other people's and knows where projects usually break.

If you already have one and it isn't working

Sometimes you don't have to change everything. You have to fix the specific piece that's failing.

If you operate in several countries

Each country has its own tax rules and its own way of doing things. Having five in the same system saves you five systems.

Common questions

Questions

Where is Zyntello based?

Zyntello, S.R.L. is a Dominican company. We operate in the Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Colombia, Guatemala and Costa Rica, and we give remote support to customers outside those countries.

Is the platform yours, or do you resell a product?

It's ours. We build and maintain it, which is what lets a needed change actually be made instead of being requested from a vendor.

Do you only work with your own platform?

No. We also do infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, custom development, technical support and specialist IT staffing. They're in the services section.

What happens to my data if I stop being a customer?

They're yours and they're handed over to you. There's a published page with the data deletion procedure and a privacy policy explaining what is kept and why.

Do you work with small companies?

Yes. In fact the per-module model exists precisely for that: so a small company can start with one piece without buying an entire system.

How do I get in touch?

Over WhatsApp at +1 829 639 9877 or by writing to info@zyntello.com. If you're already a customer, the support channel is soporte@zyntello.com.
